# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## Primary Classification by Core Mechanic

---

## 1. LOOP-DRAWING GAMES
*The primary task is to draw a single continuous closed loop*

### 1.1 Unconstrained Path Loop
Games where the loop may pass freely through cells, constrained only by clues:
- **Masyu** — loop must satisfy black/white circle turn rules
- **Slitherlink** — loop drawn between dots; numbers indicate surrounding lines
- **Yajilin** — arrow/number clues indicate black cells in a direction; loop avoids black cells

### 1.2 Directional/Wind-Constrained Loop
- **Nagareru** — wind direction in cells constrains loop movement direction

### 1.3 Gate/Sequence-Constrained Loop
- **Suraromu** — loop must pass through all "Gates" in a numbered sequence

### 1.4 Cell-Type Constrained Loop
Games where specific cell markings dictate loop behavior:
- **Dotchi-Loop** — white circles must all be turned through or all passed straight, per bold-line area; black circles excluded
- **Mid-loop** — black circles must be midpoints of straight loop segments
- **Moon-or-Sun** — loop alternates between moon-rooms and sun-rooms; visits each room once

---

## 2. CELL-SHADING / PAINTING GAMES
*The primary task is to colour or paint cells black according to constraints*

### 2.1 Connectivity & Shape Rules Only
- **Nurikabe** — numbered white islands separated by a connected black "wall"; no 2×2 black squares
- **Heyawake** — rooms with counts; painted cells non-adjacent; white cells connected and limited in cross-room runs
- **Hitori** — shade cells so no number repeats in any row/column; black cells non-adjacent; white cells connected

### 2.2 Geometric Shape Constraints on Shaded Regions
- **Choco Banana** — black regions must be rectangles/squares; white regions must not be rectangles/squares
- **Shakashaka** — triangular half-cell shading; remaining white areas must form rectangles/squares
- **Usowan** — standard adjacency shading with one deliberately wrong number per bold-line region

### 2.3 Shading with Gravity/Drop Mechanic
- **Sto-stone** — shaded stones "drop" to fill the bottom half of the grid exactly

### 2.4 Shading with Connectivity Across Regions
- **Norinori** — exactly two shaded cells per bold-line area, forming dominoes
- **LITS** — one tetromino per region; all shaded cells connected; no 2×2; same-shape tetrominoes cannot touch
- **Nuritwin** — two equal-sized shaded blocks per region; all shaded cells globally connected; no 2×2

### 2.5 Shading Guided by Numeric Clues (Non-adjacency focus)
- **Kurodoko** — numbered white cells count visible white cells in four directions; black cells non-adjacent
- **Kurotto** — circled numbers give sum of adjacent black cell runs; cells with circles stay white

### 2.6 Shading to Create a Maze
- **Nurimeizu** — paint whole rooms to create walls; shortest path S→G must pass circles and avoid triangles

---

## 3. NUMBER-PLACEMENT GAMES
*The primary task is to fill cells with numbers*

### 3.1 Latin-Square / Uniqueness Constraint
- **Sudoku** — 1–9 in every row, column, and 3×3 box

### 3.2 Region-Based Number Sets
- **Fillomino** — divide grid into blocks; each block filled with its own size number; same-size blocks non-adjacent
- **Ripple Effect** — rooms contain 1–N; duplicate numbers in a row/column must be separated by at least that number of cells
- **Makaro** — rooms contain 1–N; arrow clues indicate which adjacent cell holds the largest number; same numbers in adjacent rooms forbidden

### 3.3 Crossword-Style Number Placement
- **Nansuke** — fill white cells with numbers from a given list, reading across or down

### 3.4 Snake / Sequential Placement
- **Hebi** — place snakes (sequences 1–5) in white cells; snakes cannot touch; line-of-sight attack rules apply

---

## 4. REGION / AREA DIVISION GAMES
*The primary task is to partition the grid into regions satisfying shape or size rules*

### 4.1 Division into Rectangles
- **Shikaku** — divide into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its area

### 4.2 Division into Fixed-Size Polyominoes
- **Five Cells** — divide into pentominoes; number clues indicate boundary-line count around a cell

### 4.3 Division into L-Shaped Blocks
- **Sashigane** — divide into L-shaped (carpenter's square) blocks; circles mark bends; arrows mark ends

### 4.4 Division into Matched Pairs (Symmetric Regions)
- **Double Choco** — each block contains one white and one gray region of identical shape; numbers indicate region size

### 4.5 Division with Chaining Constraints
- **Chained Block** — black cell blocks touch only at corners (chains); no two same-shaped blocks in one chain; every block has a number or "?"

---

## 5. LINE / PATH DRAWING GAMES (Non-loop)
*The primary task is to draw lines or paths that do not form closed loops*

### 5.1 Connecting Pairs
- **Numberlink** — connect matching number pairs with non-crossing, non-overlapping lines filling all cells
- **Hashiwokakero** — connect numbered islands with 1–2 bridges; all islands form one connected network

### 5.2 Directional / Arrow-Guided Paths
- **Pencils** — identify pencil shapes and draw lines from their tips through a number of cells equal to the pencil's number

---

## 6. SYMBOL / MARK PLACEMENT GAMES
*The primary task is to place specific symbols (not numbers) into cells*

### 6.1 Light / Illumination Placement
- **Akari** — place light bulbs so every white cell is illuminated; bulbs cannot illuminate each other; numbered cells constrain adjacent bulb count

### 6.2 Directional Mark Placement
- **Juosan** — fill every cell with "—" or "|"; territory clues give difference in counts; runs limited to 2 cells in the perpendicular direction

---

## 7. OBJECT / PIECE PLACEMENT & MOVEMENT GAMES
*The primary task involves placing or moving discrete objects on the grid*

### 7.1 Movement to Target Zones
- **Satogaeri** — move circles into their home country (one per country); numbered circles move an exact distance; paths cannot cross
- **Yosenabe** — move numbered circles into gray areas; arrow paths straight and non-crossing; gray area totals must match

### 7.2 Evolving Block Placement
- **Evolomino** — place squares along arrow routes; each successive block adds one square to the previous block's shape

### 7.3 Tile Coloring to Reveal an Image
- **Tilepaint** — color whole tiles (bold-line regions) based on diagonal number clues; solution depicts an object

---

## Cross-Cutting Constraint Dimensions

| Dimension | Examples |
|---|---|
| **Connectivity required** | Nurikabe, Hitori, Kurodoko, LITS, Nuritwin |
| **No 2×2 same-color blocks** | Nurikabe, Nuritwin, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki |
| **Bold-line regions as primary structure** | Heyawake, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Double Choco, Moon-or-Sun, Sto-stone |
| **Arrow/directional clues** | Yajilin, Hebi, Sashigane, Makaro, Yosenabe |
| **Single loop constraint** | All Loop-Drawing games + Yajilin |
| **Numeric clues count neighbors** | Akari, Usowan, Kurotto, Shakashaka |
| **Path/movement non-crossing** | Numberlink, Satogaeri, Yosenabe, Hashiwokakero |

---

## Summary Tree

```
Grid-Based Logic Games
├── 1. Loop-Drawing
│   ├── 1.1 Unconstrained Path (Masyu, Slitherlink, Yajilin)
│   ├── 1.2 Directional (Nagareru)
│   ├── 1.3 Gate/Sequence (Suraromu)
│   └── 1.4 Cell-Type (Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun)
├── 2. Cell Shading/Painting
│   ├── 2.1 Connectivity & Shape (Nurikabe, Heyawake, Hitori)
│   ├── 2.2 Geometric Shape Constraints (Choco Banana, Shakashaka, Usowan)
│   ├── 2.3 Gravity Mechanic (Sto-stone)
│   ├── 2.4 Cross-Region Connectivity (Norinori, LITS, Nuritwin)
│   ├── 2.5 Numeric Line-of-Sight (Kurodoko, Kurotto)
│   └── 2.6 Maze Creation (Nurimeizu)
├── 3. Number Placement
│   ├── 3.1 Latin-Square (Sudoku)
│   ├── 3.2 Region-Based Sets (Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro)
│   ├── 3.3 Crossword-Style (Nansuke)
│   └── 3.4 Sequential/Snake (Hebi)
├── 4. Region Division
│   ├── 4.1 Rectangles (Shikaku)
│   ├── 4.2 Fixed Polyominoes (Five Cells)
│   ├── 4.3 L-Shapes (Sashigane)
│   ├── 4.4 Matched Pairs (Double Choco)
│   └── 4.5 Chained Blocks (Chained Block)
├── 5. Line/Path Drawing (Non-loop)
│   ├── 5.1 Connecting Pairs (Numberlink, Hashiwokakero)
│   └── 5.2 Arrow-Guided (Pencils)
├── 6. Symbol Placement
│   ├── 6.1 Illumination (Akari)
│   └── 6.2 Directional Marks (Juosan)
└── 7. Object Placement & Movement
    ├── 7.1 Movement to Targets (Satogaeri, Yosenabe)
    ├── 7.2 Evolving Blocks (Evolomino)
    └── 7.3 Tile Coloring (Tilepaint)
        (also: Nurimisaki — promontory/white-cell shading)
```
